gen_assessment.reasoning: Duration of dysuria (6 days) aligns with gold hpi-001, but gold includes additional burning/stinging character not mentioned here.
Gold hpi-008 notes central abdominal pain but gives no severity, intermittency, or precise suprapubic label. Pain location is supported; the 7/10 severity and intermittent pattern are added details.
Gold hpi-004 notes blood in urine but not explicitly ‘visible’ or that it lasted over the same 6 days. Presence of hematuria is supported; visibility and exact duration are added.

Generated: ‘no fever reported.’ Gold hpi-009: ‘Not feverish but not checked temp.’ and ros-005 (in generated set) presents ‘denies fever (no thermometer).’ Since we judge against gold only, gold does not explicitly state ‘no fever reported’ as a firm negative but rather lack of measurement and subjective impression; this is somewhat stronger but directionally similar. However, because gold stresses lack of checking rather than a clear negative ROS, this is best treated as a mild overstatement; classification here is closest to ADDITION, not direct contradiction.
Gold indicates patient has not checked temperature; generated treats this as a simple ‘no fever reported.’ Adds interpretive simplification not in gold.

Gold hpi-006: ‘No new PV discharge’ (implies there may be baseline discharge but no new change). Generated: ‘no vaginal discharge’ (absolute absence). This is stricter than the gold statement and conflicts with the nuance that only ‘new’ discharge was denied.

Gold hpi-011: no past history of urine infections/similar symptoms (chronic history). Generated hpi-008: no prior similar episodes (episode-focused). Closely related but not clearly identical; treated as an additional interpretive statement rather than directly supported.
No mention in any gold fact about recent exercise. Purely additional detail.

Gold hpi-010 notes no history of dehydration preceding symptoms. Generated hpi-010: no recent dehydration. Similar concept (absence of dehydration) but not clearly tied to the lead-up to symptoms as in gold; partially aligned but not exact.

Gold hpi-010: no history of frequent sexual intercourse preceding symptoms. Generated: no increase in sexual activity. Both indicate no sexual trigger, but gold refers to ‘frequent SI’ preceding symptoms; generated refers to change/increase. Overlaps but not identical in scope.

Gold lists IBS as PMH (pmh-001) but not as a separate assessment line item. ‘Stable IBS’ as a problem on the assessment is additional framing.

Gold plan-001: Nitrofurantoin 3-day course. Generated: a 3-day course of oral antibiotics for presumed UTI without naming drug. Duration and antibiotic intent supported, but the specific agent Nitrofurantoin is omitted.
No gold fact mentions the specific pharmacy or prescription routing. New detail.

Gold does not give a specific instruction about monitoring hematuria beyond general follow-up; this more detailed safety-netting about hematuria is additional.
